our method can serve a competitive alternative to maximum likelihood in estimating parameters in a location-scale model when data are censored.

the proposed method of estimating parameters of location-scale model with censored data is a good alternative to maximum likelihood estimation because of its simplicity, computational efficiency, robustness to model misspeciﬁcation, and comparable performance in terms of accuracy.

we propose a new method to estimate the location-scale model parameters with censored data and show that the asymptotical variance of our method depends on the data transformation, but the asymptotical mean square error does not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of the parameters of the location-scale model with censored data using the synthetic data approach.
the estimation of the parameters in the location–scale model when the observations are right-censored.
the estimation of location-scale models with right-censored data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this article presents a new class of estimators which is available in a closed-form and does not require an iterative method.
the estimators based on synthetic data are comparable with the maximum likelihood estimators in terms of efficiency and robustness.
the proposed method is an attractive alternative to maximum likelihood estimation in estimation for location and scale parameters when the data are randomly censored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asymptotic variance of the proposed estimators depends on the data transformation when the censoring is known but does not depend on the data transform when the censoring rate is unknown.
the proposed method is an alternative to the maximum likelihood estimation in the estimation for location-scale model with censored data, especially when the sample size is small.
our method provides an efficient alternative to the method based on maximum likelihood estimation in estimation for location–scale models with censored and right-censored data, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the method of synthetic data can be used to develop a new class of moment-based estimators for location-scale models that have desirable asymptotic properties and perform better than maximum likelihood estimation in small samples.

the use of the synthetic data approach in conjunction with moment-based methods can be a viable alternative to the use of maximum likelihood estimation in censored regression models, especially when the sample size is small or the censoring rate is relatively high.
the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators do not depend on the censoring distribution.
